summary.text: John Rutherford is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Florida's 5th District. A former Jacksonville police officer, he was elected Duval County sheriff three times before winning an open House seat in 2016. He serves on the House Appropriations Committee and is seeking another term.

paragraphs.text: Rutherford was born in Omaha, Nebraska, in 1952 and, according to his congressional biography, has lived in Jacksonville since 1958.

He earned an associate degree from Florida Junior College in 1972 and a bachelor's degree in criminology from Florida State University in 1974, and he is a graduate of the FBI National Academy (171st Session) and the National Executive Institute.
Rutherford began his law enforcement career in 1974 as a patrolman with the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office and worked his way up to sheriff.

He was elected Sheriff of Duval County in 2003, 2007, and 2011, and ran a 3,200-employee office for twelve years. His congressional biography says he emphasized intelligence-led, community-based policing and the mental-health aspects of the criminal justice system, and that he chaired the Legislative Committee of the Florida Sheriffs Association.

Rutherford won the open Florida 4th District seat in 2016, taking 38.7% in a seven-candidate Republican primary and 70.2% in the general election, and took office in January 2017. He has represented the 5th District since January 2023 and was re-elected in 2024.

According to his House website, he serves on the Appropriations Committee's Homeland Security; Military Construction, Veterans Affairs; and Transportation, Housing and Urban Development subcommittees, and he co-chairs several caucuses. Ballotpedia also lists him on the Committee on Ethics in the 119th Congress.

According to his congressional biography, Rutherford has been married to his wife, Pat, for 53 years. They have two children, six grandchildren, and three great-grandchildren, and they attend Assumption Catholic Church in Jacksonville.
